ca_locomotion_rock.blurb: A small, low formation inside Joshua Tree's Real Hidden Valley, and one of the gentler spots in the valley for learning to lead. Most of the dozen routes are trad cracks, with a couple of top-rope lines. Grades run mostly from easy fifth class through 5.8, with a handful of harder lines from 5.9 up to 5.11. The face is coarse and gravelly, so tape is worth packing. The climbs start in a shallow crevice that gives a bit of shade between laps, and the walk from the lot follows the nature trail. A friendly stop before heading to the valley's harder classics.

ca_monkey_face.blurb: A dark granite wall that is the first one you meet on entering Monkeyface Falls, a slot canyon off Highway 38 in the San Bernardino Mountains. All twelve routes are bolted sport lines, mostly moderate with the bulk around 5.7, plus a few 5.10s and one harder pitch. The lines are fairly long and reward tidy footwork, and small falls trickle behind the belay. The wall faces south and catches sun most of the day, so it suits the cooler months best; once it warms past about 70 degrees it gets uncomfortable. The shaded canyon beyond is the summer alternative.

ca_motherlode_rock_west_face.blurb: A steep wall in the Central Pinnacles of Holcomb Valley, in the San Bernardino Mountains above Big Bear, at roughly 7,500 feet. Of its twelve routes, ten are bolted and two are trad. Nearly everything falls between 5.9 and 5.11, centered on 5.10, so this is a wall for climbers past the beginner stage. The face comes in two sections: the left side rises out of a rocky gully, while the right side starts from level ground. Pitches are short, around 40 feet on the one measured here, with edges, bulges and a few dike features. The walk in from the trail system is brief.

ca_main_wall_9.blurb: The main face of Tick Rock, a small roadside crag tucked into the Pacific Palisades neighborhood between Santa Monica and Malibu. Eleven of the twelve routes are bolted, with one trad line. Grades cluster around 5.10, with a couple of 5.8s, several 5.12s and a single 5.13. The sandstone is fractured and fine grained, and the terrain mixes steep bolted faces, slabs and crack finishes. The wall gets shade for part of the day and stays cool in summer, which makes it a good half-day outing. The base is only a short steep trail from the road.

ca_dutzi_rock.blurb: A large south-facing formation at the northern edge of The Outback, in the Hidden Valley area of Joshua Tree National Park. Of its twelve routes, nine are trad and three are top-rope. Grades range from an easy 5.6 through the 5.9 and 5.10 range up to several 5.11s. Some of the easier leads give newer leaders decent gear and rests, though at least one is described as less appealing than it looks. Reach the base by scrambling up through boulders. With a south-facing wall it takes plenty of sun.

ca_frontier_right.blurb: The first dome you reach at Little Egypt, a cluster of granite crack crags near Bishop in the Eastern Sierra, at about 6,600 feet. Climbs here are single pitch, around 100 to 150 feet, and mostly trad, with three bolted lines among the twelve. Grades span 5.8 to 5.11 with one much harder line, centered on 5.10. Expect clean cracks from fingers to fists plus some grainy face moves, and bring tape. The wall faces west, so summer afternoons get hot; early or late starts are better. It is usually far quieter than the nearby Buttermilks.

ca_fraggle_rock.blurb: A remote formation on the eastern ridge of the Desert Queen Mine area in Joshua Tree's Queen Valley, and the farthest of the crags from the parking. Twelve routes, two thirds trad and the rest bolted, from one easy scramble to a few 5.12s; the bulk sit between 5.9 and 5.11. Most lines face west or north, so mornings and early afternoon stay shaded. The walk is long by Joshua Tree standards but passes old mine tunnels and tailings and ends at a miner's cabin below the rock. The area feels out of the way and quiet.
ca_fraggle_rock.approach: A long walk compared with most Joshua Tree crags, since this is the farthest formation from the parking. The trail passes old mine workings and tailings and ends at a miner's cabin at the base of the rock.
